function.name: EventSettingsApi_create_website_alert_config
function.description: Creates a configuration for website alerting within the system, allowing users to define conditions under which alerts should be triggered for a website. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

name.description: The name for the website alert configuration.

description.description: A detailed description for the website alert configuration.

severity.description: The severity level of the alert when triggered.

triggering.description: Flag indicating whether the alert configuration should also trigger an incident.

websiteId.description: The unique identifier of the website for which the alert configuration is created.

tagFilterExpression.description: A boolean expression used to filter the scope of website beacons based on tags.

granularity.description: The evaluation granularity in seconds used for detection of threshold violations.

rule.description: The type of rule this alert configuration pertains to, such as 'traffic spike' or 'downtime'.

threshold.description: The threshold value that, when exceeded, will trigger the alert. This is a float type value.

timeThreshold.description: The time duration in seconds during which the threshold must be exceeded to trigger the alert.

alertChannelIds.description: A list of alert channel IDs defined in Instana to which the alert notifications will be sent.

I’m afraid I don’t have direct visibility into “delta”’s current Instana Alert deployment – there isn’t a built‑in query you can run against our chat interface that pulls out the exact software release numbers your team’s using. However, you can quickly discover that information yourself through one of two common paths: | Method | What you’ll see | How to get it | |--------|-----------------|---------------| | **Instana UI** | *Version* field at the top right corner of the dashboard (or in Settings → About) | Log in to the web console, click the gear icon → `About`. It lists the full build ID (`instana-agent-x.y.z`), the Java runtime, and the underlying OS/architecture. | | **API / CLI** | Same build metadata exposed programmatically | • Use the REST endpoint `/api/v1/system/info`
• Run `curl -u USER:PWD https:///api/v1/system/info`
• Look for fields like `"agent_version"`, `"java_runtime"` and `"os_info"`. | If you’re specifically interested in the **event‑settings** side of things—i.e., which alert rules are active—you could pull those definitions too: ```bash curl -X GET \ -H "Accept: application/json" \ -u USER:PWD \ https:///api/v2/event-settings/api/createWebsiteAlertConfig ``` That returns all configured alert configs, including their `version` tag if you’ve added one manually. If you haven’t tagged them, you won’t see a separate “version” per rule; instead each rule inherits whatever agent/build version is currently running on the host(s). --- ### Quick checklist for verifying the environment 1. **Check the Agent logs** On the machine where the Instana Agent runs, look at `/var/log/instana/agent.log` (Linux) or `%ProgramData%\Instana\Agent\logs\agent.log` (Windows). The first few lines contain something like: ``` [INFO] Starting Instana Agent v5.12.7 (build #12345) ``` 2. **Verify the Docker image/tag** If you’re deploying agents inside containers, inspect the image tag: ```bash docker images | grep instana ``` You’ll typically see entries like `instana/agent:v5.12.7`. 3. **Cross‑check with the Deployment Pipeline** Your CI/CD pipeline usually pins the agent version in its Helm chart values or Kubernetes manifests. Search for `image.tag:` or similar keys in your repo. Once you locate the specific build identifiers, you can map them back to the official Instana release notes to confirm feature sets, bug fixes, and security patches applicable to that version. Let me know if you’d like help automating any part of this process—for example, scripting a quick inventory across multiple hosts—or if you suspect a particular component (e.g., the Webhook integration) is behind a different minor revision than the rest of the stack.
